title: Ravana entices Seetha to marry him
introduction: Ravana entices Seetha to marry him by demonstrating various luxuries and comforts, and even baiting her to become his empress. The words of Ravana have some latent meanings as derived by ancient commentators and they are included here, as far as possible.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे पंच पंचाशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 55th chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
संदिश्य राक्षसान् घोरान् रावणो अष्टौ महाबलान् |
आत्मानम् बुद्धि वैक्लव्यात् कृत कृत्यम् अमन्यत
verses.iast:
sandiśya rākṣasān ghorān rāvaṇo aṣṭau mahābalān |
ātmānam buddhi vaiklavyāt kṛta kṛtyam amanyata
verses.translation: On directing those eight ghastly demons Ravana is amused in his heart of hearts that he has accomplished a great feat.

verses.devanagari:
स चिंतयानो वैदेहीम् काम बाण संप्रपीडितः |
प्रविवेश गृहम् रम्यम् सीताम् द्रष्टुम् अभित्वरन्
verses.iast:
sa ciṃtayāno vaidehīm kāma bāṇa samprapīḍitaḥ |
praviveśa gṛham ramyam sītām draṣṭum abhitvaran
verses.translation: On continually musing upon Vaidehi Ravana is tormented with the arrows of Love-god, thereby to lay eyes on Seetha he post-hastily entered the beautiful palace.

glosses.meaning: by Love-god's, arrows, very, much, tormented
at Seetha, to lay eyes on, post, hastily

verses.devanagari:
स प्रविश्य तु तत् वेश्म रावणो राक्षस अधिपः |
अपश्यत् राक्षसी मध्ये सीताम् दुःख परायणम्
verses.iast:
sa praviśya tu tat veśma rāvaṇo rākṣasa adhipaḥ |
apaśyat rākṣasī madhye sītām duḥkha parāyaṇam
verses.translation: On entering the palace-chamber that supremo of demons beheld Seetha overwhelmed with ruefulness amongst demonesses.

verses.devanagari:
अश्रु पूर्ण मुखीम् दीनाम् शोक भार अवपीडिताम् |
वायु वेगैः इव आक्रांताम् मज्जन्तीम् नावम् अर्णवे
मृग यूथ परिभ्रष्टाम् मृगीम् श्वभिः इव आवृताम् |
अधोगत मुखीम् सीताम् ताम् अभ्येत्य निशाचरः
ताम् तु शोक वशात् दीनाम् अवशाम् राक्षस अधिपः |
स बलात् दर्शयामास गृहम् देव गृह उपमम्
verses.iast:
aśru pūrṇa mukhīm dīnām śoka bhāra avapīḍitām |
vāyu vegaiḥ iva ākrāṃtām majjantīm nāvam ar.hṇave
mṛga yūtha paribhraṣṭām mṛgīm śvabhiḥ iva āvṛtām |
adhogata mukhīm sītām tām abhyetya niśācaraḥ
tām tu śoka vaśāt dīnām avaśām rākṣasa adhipaḥ |
sa balāt darśayāmāsa gṛham deva gṛha upamam
verses.translation: She whose visage is brimming over with tears, one browbeaten and downtrodden with the burden of bewail, one capsized like a boat that is about to capsize in an ocean spreadeagled with whirlwinds, and one alike an impala altogether swerved from its herd of impala yet hemmed in with dog-wolves, that nightwalker came nigh of such a Seetha whose face is downcast unwilling to see any, and to such a pitiable Seetha who is in the shackles of her sorrow, that supremo of demons compellingly started to show his palace which is similar to any paradisiacal palace.
notes: Then he must have hauled her by her hand or demonesses must have dragged all along the corridors, chambers and all over, or as usual, he must have carried her on his flank to show his palace. Taking this situation and the statement at verse 1, ātmānam buddhi vaiklavyāt Rama Tilaka negates the idea that Seetha is brought to Lanka as a much cherished Goddess Lakshmi, but her bringing is only with a villainous intent. Even then, the supporters of Ravana - the devotee - disagree. There are many such slants given to Ravana's dialogs, to portray him as a devotee, in this chapter itself.

glosses.meaning: about to sink [about to capsize,] boat, who is alike
of sorrow, by shackles, pitiable one [Seetha]

verses.devanagari:
हर्म्य प्रासाद संबधम् स्त्री सहस्र निषेवितम् |
नाना पक्षि गणैः जुष्टम् नाना रत्न समन्वितम्
दान्तकैः तापनीयैः च स्फाटिकै राजतैः तथा |
वज्र वैदूर्य चित्रैः च स्तम्भैः दृष्टि मनोरमैः
दिव्य दुन्दुभि निर्घोषम् तप्त कांचन भूषणम् |
verses.iast:
harmya prāsāda sambadham strī sahasra niṣevitam |
nānā pakṣi gaṇaiḥ juṣṭam nānā ratna samanvitam
dāntakaiḥ tāpanīyaiḥ ca sphāṭikai rājataiḥ tathā |
vajra vaidūrya citraiḥ ca stambhaiḥ dṛṣṭi manoramaiḥ
divya dundubhi nir.hghoṣam tapta kāṃcana bhūṣaṇam |
verses.translation: That paradisiacal mansion house of Decahedral Ravana is congestive with innumerable cupolaed skyscrapers, adored with thousands of females, frequented by diverse bevies of birds, and it comprised of numerous gemstones. The pillars are amazingly gilded with engraving of ivory, gilt, quartz, silvern linocuts, and they are even embossed with diamonds and with lapis gems, which are heart-pleasing for a look. The drumbeats of divine drums are echoing in entire palace, and its archways are adorned with the gildings of pure gold.

glosses.meaning: that paradisiacal palace like mansion house of Decahedral Ravana
amazingly, [ellipt. glided, gild the lily type] also
for a look, for hearts, pleasing

verses.devanagari:
सोपानम् कांचनम् चित्रम् आरुरोह तया सह
दान्तका राजताः चैव गवाक्षाः प्रिय दर्शनाः |
हेम जाला आवृताः च आसन् तत्र प्रासाद पंक्तयः
verses.iast:
sopānam kāṃcanam citram āruroha tayā saha
dāntakā rājatāḥ caiva gavākṣāḥ priya darśanāḥ |
hema jālā āvṛtāḥ ca āsan tatra prāsāda paṃk{}tayaḥ
verses.translation: Ravana walked up the wonderful golden staircase along with Seetha, and the rows of skyscrapers with windows that are ivoried and silvered and with window-blinds are seen from the windows of the landing on that flight of stairs, which are also ivoried and silvered windows with window-blinds, and all are amusing for sight.
notes: Did she walk on her own or was she dragged on the flight of stairs? Yes! She had to walk up the staircase after Ravana, but defiantly and straggly.

glosses.meaning: skyscraper, rows of[ aasan = are there.

verses.devanagari:
सुधा मणि विचित्राणि भूमि भागानि सर्वशः |
दशग्रीवः स्व भवने प्रादर्शयत मैथिलीम्
verses.iast:
sudhā maṇi vicitrāṇi bhūmi bhāgāni sarvaśaḥ |
daśagrīvaḥ sva bhavane prādarśayata maithilīm
verses.translation: That Decahedral Ravana displayed the multiple stories of his own palace which is all over white-marbled and diamond encrusted to Maithili.

glosses.meaning: white [whitewashed, or, white-marbled] maNi vicitraaNi = diamond [encrusted,] amazing

verses.devanagari:
दीर्घिकाः पुष्करिण्यः च नाना पुष्प समावृताः |
रावणो दर्शयामास सीताम् शोक परायणाम्
verses.iast:
dīrghikāḥ puṣkariṇyaḥ ca nānā puṣpa samāvṛtāḥ |
rāvaṇo darśayāmāsa sītām śoka parāyaṇām
verses.translation: Ravana continued to display the descendible wellsprings and leisure pools from which diverse flowers have sprung and overspread them, regardless of Seetha's languishing under her anguish.
notes: Has she seen all these riches of Ravana? Yes! She had seen, but in disdain and scorn. Refraining and desisting from allurement is possible only on seeing the objects of lure. And yielding to such an opulent demon or his opulence, just for the sake of carnality, is beyond the scope of Seetha's thinking according to her reply to Ravana, in next chapter 'all this affluence is going to be reduced to ashes...' keeping Rama in view as the reducing agent, for Hanuma, the actual reducer of this affluence, is yet an unknown entity.

glosses.meaning: diverse, flowers, overspread with, leisure pools

verses.devanagari:
दर्शयित्वा तु वैदेहीम् कृत्स्नम् तत् भवन उत्तमम् |
उवाच वाक्यम् पापात्मा सीताम् लोभितुम् इच्छया
verses.iast:
dar.hśayitvā tu vaidehīm kṛtsnam tat bhavana uttamam |
uvāca vākyam pāpātmā sītām lobhitum icchayā
verses.translation: On flaunting his best palace in its entirety to Vaidehi that dirty-minded Ravana spoke this sentence to Seetha in order that she may be tempted on her own, lustily.

glosses.meaning: to Vaidehi, on flaunting siitaam icChayaa lobhitum = Seetha, by lust, in order to tempt

verses.devanagari:
दश राक्षस कोट्यः च द्वाविंशतिः अथ अपराः |
वर्जयित्वा जरा वृद्धान् बालान् च रजनीचरान्
तेषाम् प्रभुः अहम् सीते सर्वेषाम् भीम कर्मणाम् |
verses.iast:
daśa rākṣasa koṭyaḥ ca dvāviṃśatiḥ atha aparāḥ |
var.hjayitvā jarā vṛddhān bālān ca rajanīcarān
teṣām prabhuḥ aham sīte sarveṣām bhīma karmaṇām |
verses.translation: "Oh, Seetha, ten crores of first-rated demons are there, furthermore, twenty-two crores of demons of ghastly exploits are there, thus all put together, three hundred twenty millions of demons are there in Lanka, omitting the weakish, oldish, youngish demons. For all of them I am the lord." Thus Ravana started his self-eulogy.

glosses.meaning: for demons, , crores of - for ten crores of demons are there
two, twenty [twenty-two crores are there - total ten twenty two = thirty three crores of demons are there]

verses.devanagari:
सहस्रम् एकम् एकस्य मम कार्य पुरःसरम्
यत् इदम् राज्य तंत्रम् मे त्वयि सर्वम् प्रतिष्ठितम् |
जीवितम् च विशालाक्षि त्वम् मे प्राणैः गरीयसी
verses.iast:
sahasram ekam ekasya mama kārya puraḥsaram
yat idam rājya taṃtram me tvayi sarvam pratiṣṭhitam |
jīvitam ca viśālākṣi tvam me prāṇaiḥ garīyasī
verses.translation: "For every single work of mine a thousand servitors will rush in. Such as I am I pledge entire life of mine along with the suzerainty of this sovereign city-state Lanka to you, oh, broad-eyed lady, for you are loftier than my lives.

glosses.meaning: work, will be ahead of - will rush in
which, this, sovereignty's, suzerainty is there
in you, is pledged - a thing given as a token of love, favour, or something to come
you are, to me, by lives, loftier.

verses.devanagari:
बह्वीनाम् उत्तम स्त्रीणाम् मम यो असौ परिग्रहः |
तासाम् त्वम् ईश्वरी सीते मम भार्या भव प्रिये
verses.iast:
bahvīnām uttama strīṇām mama yo asau parigrahaḥ |
tāsām tvam īśvarī sīte mama bhāryā bhava priye
verses.translation: "Oh, Seetha, you will become an empress for all of the those countless females of finest fabric amassed by me, oh, dear, if only you marry me.
notes: dhvani/innuendo: Ravana the devotee is saying: 'oh, Seetha... you become my empress and lord over me and all of my wives that are amassed by me... for, You are the most adorable Goddess Lakshmi, and now though appearing in a gross form of Seetha, you are the real Subtlety, Goddess Lakshmi... bhāryā; bhā= cidrūpiṇī= oh, Subtlety; āryā = oh, adorable one; a+bhava = oh, Redeemer; priye = most adorable Goddess Lakshmi.'

glosses.meaning: which, this, capturing, [or, marrying, or amassing]
mine, wife, you become [if only you become.]

verses.devanagari:
साधु किम् ते अन्यया बुद्ध्या रोचयस्व वचो मम |
भजस्व मा अभितप्तस्य प्रसादम् कर्तुम् अर्हसि
verses.iast:
sādhu kim te anyayā buddhyā rocayasva vaco mama |
bhajasva mā abhitaptasya prasādam kartum ar.hhasi
verses.translation: "You be keen on my amiable words and it will be apt of you to show compassion on me, for I have burning desire for you, and of what use is your thinking conversely about that long-lost Rama?
notes: dhvani/innuendo: The word kāma is ellipted here as it appears in other mms. Then it is said ' kāma 'desirous... I have the burning desire of regaining my servitude at your door...' thus mām bhajasva 'me, you accept accordingly...'

glosses.meaning: by converse, thinking, what [is the use]
[in desire,] one who is burning with
compassion, to do [to show,] apt of you.

verses.devanagari:
परिक्षिप्ता समुद्रेण लंका इयम् शत योजना |
न इयम् धर्षयितुम् शक्या स इन्द्रैः अपि सुर असुरैः
verses.iast:
parikṣiptā samudreṇa laṃkā iyam śata yojanā |
na iyam dhar.hṣayitum śakyā sa indraiḥ api sura asuraiḥ
verses.translation: "It is impossible to assail this Lanka even for Indra with all of the gods and demons, as an ocean roundly enshrouds this Lanka which is hundred-yojana-s witdthwise.

verses.devanagari:
न देवेषु न यक्षेषु न गंधर्वेषु न ऋषिषु |
अहम् पश्यामि लोकेषु यो मे वीर्य समो भवेत्
verses.iast:
na deveṣu na yakṣeṣu na gaṃdharveṣu na ṛṣiṣu |
aham paśyāmi lokeṣu yo me vīrya samo bhavet
verses.translation: "I behold none matchable to my vitality is existent among gods; among yaksha-s - no; among gandharva-s - no; among sages - no, nor anyone in any world.

glosses.meaning: he who, mine, vitality, equal [matchable to]

verses.devanagari:
राज्य भ्रष्टेन दीनेन तापसेन पदातिना |
किम् करिष्यसि रामेण मानुषेण अल्प तेजसा
verses.iast:
rājya bhraṣṭena dīnena tāpasena padātinā |
kim kariṣyasi rāmeṇa mānuṣeṇa alpa tejasā
verses.translation: "What can you achieve with that dethroned, hapless, seer, vagrant Rama who is short-lived, for after all, he is a human with littlest vitality?
notes: dhvani/innuendo: Ravana, the devotee is saying: 'Why this wasteful lamenting about an un-lamentable entity, called Rama, for he is rājya bhraṣṭa yena 'by whom enemies are dethroned...' rājyāt bhrṣṭā ripavo yasmāt tena and take this as one word dīnenatāpasenagatāyuṣā by which I mean... dīna ina tāpasa ina gata āyuṣā where ina means 'lord...' thus a lord of hapless, a lord for seers, and mānuṣeṇa gatāyuṣā whereby 'for a man who gained longevity...' that is ekā daśa sahasra samvatsara parimita āyuṣa yena gataḥ - prāptaḥ, saḥ 'one who has achieved eleven thousands years of age in human incarnation...' in which he has to lord over and save the saints, sages, seers and such hapless lot...' and alpa tejasā by which I mean alpam itareṣām teejo yasmāt tena 'by whom others' resplendency is dwindled and lessened, just by his own resplendence... about such rāmeṇa kim? Why you bother about such Rama, since he is parama puruṣa the Supreme Person?

glosses.meaning: with [the one who is] from kingdom, overthrown [dethroned]

verses.devanagari:
भजस्व सीते माम् एव भर्ता अहम् सदृशः तव |
यौवनम् हि अध्रुवम् भीरु रमस्व इह मया सह
verses.iast:
bhajasva sīte mām eva bhartā aham sadṛśaḥ tava |
yauvanam hi adhruvam bhīru ramasva iha mayā saha
verses.translation: "Oh, Seetha, you apotheosise me only for I am your seemliest husband, oh, jumpy lady, indeed, primeness has impermanence, thus here you be blithesome with me.
notes: dhvani/innuendo: Ravana, the devotee is saying, me yauvanam 'my lifespan...' where the word yauvana indicates total lifespan from childhood, to young age, to old age... 'Thereby the total lifespan of mine is a + dhruvam 'impermanent...' life itself is impermanent... and with elliptic yataḥ 'whereby...' aham tava sadṛśaḥ 'I am your seemliest... bhartā; bibharti śuśrūṣa ādinā svāminam iti bharta= sevakaḥ 'a servant...' and with elliptic ataḥ 'thereby...' mā bhajava 'me alone, you deify, as un-godly beings cannot be in the service of Goddess Lakshmi... take me as your servant...' māmeva= mā ava 'me, deliver... accord deliverance...' for that you stay here in Lanka maya saha which cleaves like mā= lakśmi, rājya lakśmi 'with Fortune of Kingdom...' saha 'along with...' ramasva 'you grace us...'

'Whereby my lifespan is impermanent to adore you, thereby you deify me from this accursed being to be in your service constantly... for which I am the seemliest servant of yours... for that you stay in Lanka and grace me and this Fortune of Kingdom, till the arrival of Rama, and then accord deliverance through Rama...

verses.devanagari:
दर्शने मा कृथाः बुद्धिम् राघवस्य वरानने |
का अस्य शक्तिः इह आगंतुम् अपि सीते मनोरथैः
verses.iast:
dar.hśane mā kṛthāḥ buddhim rāghavasya varānane |
kā asya śaktiḥ iha āgaṃtum api sīte manorathaiḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, beautifully visaged lady, it is needless to have half a mind to see that Raghava, oh, Seetha, even if his wits chariot him what is his calibre to come thither crossing an un-crossable ocean?
notes: dhvani/innuendo: Rama is living by his own wits and wisdom to come to Lanka, and his chariot called heart, is ambitiously steered by that chariot's horses, called the five senses of Rama, towards Lanka alone all through this incarnation. And bechanced is that time and opportunity, thus he has to come here, hence oh, Seetha, you needn't worry...

glosses.meaning: mind, do not, do [do not half a half mind, needless to think]
by his, thought [wits,] by chariot, even - even by his thinking he cannot come here

verses.devanagari:
न शक्यो वायुः आकाशे पाशैः बद्धम् महाजवः |
दीप्यमानस्य वा अपि अग्नेः ग्रहीतुम् विमलाम् शिखाम्
verses.iast:
na śakyo vāyuḥ ākāśe pāśaiḥ baddham mahājavaḥ |
dīpyamānasya vā api agneḥ grahītum vimalām śikhām
verses.translation: "It is impossible to knot the currents of cyclonic gusts in mid air, more so, it is impracticable to lay hold on the tongues of radiately irradiant fire.

glosses.meaning: in mid air, with ropes, to knot
even, or [more so,] to lay hold of

verses.devanagari:
त्रयाणाम् अपि लोकानाम् न तम् पश्यामि शोभने |
विक्रमेण नयेत् यः त्वाम् मत् बाहु परिपालिताम्
verses.iast:
trayāṇām api lokānām na tam paśyāmi śobhane |
vikrameṇa nayet yaḥ tvām mat bāhu paripālitām
verses.translation: "Oh, benefactress of bliss, he who can lead you back with his valour, while you are being fended off by my mighty arms, him I do not envisage even in any one world of this threefold world.
notes: dhvani/innuendo: 'Who can manaḥ rathaiḥ api wishfully iha āgantum enter this Lanka, and if tried, he becomes a straw in the gale or char in flame... hence tam na paśyāmi I don't foresee anyone else... rāmam vinā, iti seṣaḥ 'excepting Rama...' ellipted. Thus, Rama is scheduled to come here as we have our own dealings, hence mā kṛthāḥ buddhim darśane rāmasya don't get perturbed at mind in not seeing Rama... he comes soon...'

glosses.meaning: by my, [mighty] arms, fended off, you

verses.devanagari:
लंकायाम् सुमहत् राज्यम् इदम् त्वम् अनुपालय |
त्वत् प्रेष्या मत् विधा चैव देवाः च अपि चर अचरम्
verses.iast:
laṃkāyām sumahat rājyam idam tvam anupālaya |
tvat preṣyā mat vidhā caiva devāḥ ca api cara acaram
verses.translation: "You rule over this very great empire of Lanka as an empress of Lanka, while me and mine, also thus all gods like me who hitherto are under my rule, and all mobile and sessile entities of whom I am the ruler, they too will hereafter make ourselves useful as your royal stewards, if you marry me.
notes: From now on Ravana is dedicating whatever he has or acquired to his benefactress, Goddess Lakshmi. By saying madvidhā 'me-like...' it is ātma samarpaṇa self-dedication...' lankāyām rājyam anu pālaya 'from Lanka you rule over...' this is ātmīya samarpaṇa 'selfless dedication...'

verses.devanagari:
अभिषेक उदक क्लिन्ना तुष्टा च रमयस्व माम् |
दुष्कृतम् यत् पुरा कर्म वन वासेन तद् गतम्
यत् च ते सुकृतो धर्मः तस्य इह फलम् आप्नुहि |
verses.iast:
abhiṣeka udaka klinnā tuṣṭā ca ramayasva mām |
duṣkṛtam yat purā karma vana vāsena tad gatam
yat ca te sukṛto dharmaḥ tasya iha phalam āpnuhi |
verses.translation: "Wet with the waters of anointment you be elated and then delight me. By your damnable dwelling in forests bygone is your bad-luck that you misdealt in bygone times. And what dutiable good deed is to be done by you in marrying me, you do that now, and secure the fruits of that good deed here by marrying me.
notes: dhvani/innuendo: 'A damnable demon living in vana vāsena where vana is to betaken as waters, 'suchlike me living in an island surrounded by oceanic waters...' mayā, iti śeṣaḥ ellipted 'by me...' purā yat duṣkṛtam karma - kṛtam iti śeṣaḥ 'earlier what sinful act...' ellipted 'was done...' tat= duṣkarma; tava= mama iṣṭa devatā darśana mātreṇa - gataḥ 'that sin - just by the chance of seeing my choicest deity Goddess Lakshmi - it has gone...' purā maya sukṛto yo dharmaḥ 'by which good deed I have done earlier...' tasya phalam 'its good results...' te - nivedayāmi 'I surrender unto you... tat āpnuhi 'that you kindly accept...'

'As a damnable and islanded demon living amidst water surrounded island, what all the evil-acts done by me are evanished just by getting a glimpse of my choicest deity Goddess Lakshmi in you, thus I am absolved of all demerits... and any merit, if remnant with me by my performing some good deeds, intentionally or unintentionally, I surrender the fruits of all those merits even, unto to you... pray accept...'

glosses.meaning: that, in forests, by dwelling, is bygone
your, which, well-done, dutiable [to become my empress]
its [that deed's,] fruit, here, you secure.

verses.devanagari:
इह सर्वाणि माल्यानि दिव्य गंधानि मैथिलि
भूषणानि च मुख्यानि तानि सेव मया सह |
verses.iast:
iha sar.hvāṇi mālyāni divya gaṃdhāni maithili
bhūṣaṇāni ca mukhyāni tāni seva mayā saha |
verses.translation: "Oh, Maithili, here all the garlands are divinely fragranced and the jewellery is topmost, you will dress up with them along with me should you become my wife.
notes: dhvani/innuendo: A woman is attractable by embellishments and nothing is uncommon about it. A commonplace devotee offers just a leaf, or a mere fruit, or at least water to his deity as Bhagavad Gita said: phalam, puṣpam, toyam 'a fruit, a leaf or water is enough to satisfy God...' since a mountainous God cannot be appeased with mountainy offerings. But here Ravana, the devotee wants to embellish his deity with divinely garlands and topmost jewellery... maya - samarpitāni iti śeṣaḥ 'by me...' ellipted: 'offered...' saha= ekadaiva 'at least once...' sevasva 'accept them...' 'Touch my offerings at least for once... thereby I deem that I am graced by you...'

glosses.meaning: make use of - you dress up with them.

verses.devanagari:
पुष्पकम् नाम सुश्रोणि भ्रातुः वैश्रवणस्य मे
विमानम् सूर्य संकाशम् तरसा निर्जितम् रणे |
verses.iast:
puṣpakam nāma suśroṇi bhrātuḥ vaiśravaṇasya me
vimānam sūrya saṃkāśam tarasā nirjitam raṇe |
verses.translation: "Oh, well-waisted lady, just by my might I notched up an aircraft known as Pushpaka from my brother Kubera in a war with him, which is similar sun in its shine. [3-55-29b. 30a]

glosses.meaning: by might, [by me,] notched up, in war.

verses.devanagari:
विशालम् रमणीयम् च तत् विमानम् मनो जवम्
तत्र सीते मया सार्धम् विहरस्व यथा सुखम् |
verses.iast:
viśālam ramaṇīyam ca tat vimānam mano javam
tatra sīte mayā sārdham viharasva yathā sukham |
verses.translation: "That aircraft is expansive and exhilarating, also its speed is on par with intuition, oh, Seetha, in that you can cheerfully fly about along with me, should you marry me.
notes: dhvani/innuendo: 'That aircraft maya - samarpite - iti śeṣaḥ when I dedicated that aircraft to you...' sa artham= sarva sampadbhiḥ 'with all other riches, besides this aircraft... viharasva 'you enjoy...' 'Apart from this aircraft, I denounce all the riches I gained in you... you enjoy the fruits of my action and release me...'

glosses.meaning: as per, [your] cheer [cheerfully,] you fly about.

verses.devanagari:
वदनम् पद्म संकाशम् विमलम् चारु दर्शनम्
शोक आर्तम् तु वरारोहे न भ्राजति वर आनने |
verses.iast:
vadanam padma saṃkāśam vimalam cāru darśanam
śoka ārtam tu varārohe na bhrājati vara ānane |
verses.translation: "Oh, lady with a comely countenance, your visage is lotus similar in its shine, besides being immaculate, fairish and eyeful, but oh, curvaceous lady, with such a mushily maudlin of such a face this palace of mine is unbright, thus marry me to brighten everything" Thus Ravana spoke to Seetha.

verses.devanagari:
एवम् वदति तस्मिन् सा वस्त्र अन्तेन वर अंगना
पिधाय इन्दु निभम् सीता मंदम् अश्रून् अवर्तयत् |
verses.iast:
evam vadati tasmin sā vastra antena vara aṃganā
pidhāya indu nibham sītā maṃdam aśrūn avartayat |
verses.translation: While Ravana is speaking to her in this way that graceful lady Seetha veiled her moonier face with fringe of her sari, and stiflingly dispelled tears on that mooniest face behind her half-veil.

glosses.meaning: by him [Ravana, thus, she is spoken

verses.devanagari:
ध्यायन्तीम् ताम् इव अस्वस्थाम् सीताम् चिंता हत प्रभाम्
उवाच वचनम् वीरो रावणो रजनी चरः |
verses.iast:
dhyāyantīm tām iva asvasthām sītām ciṃtā hata prabhām
uvāca vacanam vīro rāvaṇo rajanī caraḥ |
verses.translation: To her who is disconcerted and whose anguish marred her brilliance and who is appearing as though pondering over the question of her submittal to Ravana, or otherwise, although she is meditating, to such a Seetha Ravana the nightwalker said these words.
notes: She allowed him to prattle whatever he wished, but when it is aimed at her face, she had to veil it customarily to conceal the flood of sobbing tears, aversely. But Ravana, being a leech of lechery, amusedly thinks that she is bashful, thus silent, and because silence is 'half-agreeing', thus he furthers his leeching.

glosses.meaning: meditating [appearing to be pondering over,] as if - she appeared

verses.devanagari:
अलम् व्रीडेन वैदेहि धर्म लोप कृतेन ते
आर्षो अयम् देवि निष्यन्दो यः त्वाम् अभिगमिष्यति |
verses.iast:
alam vrīḍena vaidehi dharma lopa kṛtena te
ārṣo ayam devi niṣyando yaḥ tvām abhigamiṣyati |
verses.translation: "Oh, Vaidehi, enough is this embarrassment of yours presuming that your consorting with me is detrimental to scriptural canons, oh, empress, what that is approaching you in the form of queen-hood is absolutely compatible with the tradition.
notes: dhvani/innuendo: 'Enough is this embarrassment alam vrīdena in the matter of 'served and servant..' ayam daiva niṣṣyandaḥ for this is preordained by gods... ārṣaḥ 'age old, traditional, and perennial...' tvām abhigamiṣyati 'the same 'served and servant relation' is now approaching you... in this incarnation and nothing new about it, for this is preordained by gods, age old, perennial, and traditional, thus enough with your embarrassment... and accept me as your devotee...' Maheshvara Tiirtha.

Much is commented on this verse and this verse itself is held controversial as the meaning for niṣyandaḥ as 'connection...' is said to be ill defined. Further, some versions use differently as shown above. It is said that yet another ancient mms of Ramayana contains the same verse as: alam vrīḍena vaidehi dharma tāpa kṛtena ca | harṣo ayam devi vispaṣṭo yaḥ tvām upagamiṣyati || where the first foot is almost the same and the second foot: harṣo ayam devi vispaṣṭo yaḥ tvām upagamiṣyati which means devi oh, lady yaḥ harṣaḥ which pleasure you are going to get with your queen-hood tvām upagamiṣyati to you approaching in the mode of queen-hood ayam harṣaḥ vispaṣṭaḥ that pleasure is evident...

'Oh, Lady, which pleasure you are going to get as a queen, for that queen-hood is fast approaching you, that pleasure is evident... why then you presume that marrying me is anti-canonical, and thus be ashamed...' so said Ravana with a kind of epicurean philosophy.

A woman who marries twice is called punarbhuḥ and these are of three kinds. And then there is another type called svairiṇi. The first category are the women who leave off their first husbands and get married to another, thus become the first punarbhuḥ and the svairiṇi is the kind of women who will not care customs but follow their own course of alliances. para pūrvāḥ striyaḥ tvat anyāḥ sapta proktā svayambhuvā | punarbhūḥ trividhā tāsām tu svairiṇī catur vidhā || nārada Then Ravana is supposed to have argued with Seetha 'you become a punarbhuḥ or choose whatever kind of scriptural statement about the rules of remarriages, but marry me - Govindaraja.

There is another kind of Indian marriage called rākśasa vivāha loosely: 'demonical marriage...' i.e., abducting a girl with her consent and marrying secretly. But this way of rākśasa vivāha 'marriage through abduction...' is admissible only to unmarried girls but not to the married women. Hence, the scriptural canons again cannot be satisfied. Therefore Ravana is said to have stated all this as an eyewash due to his tamo guṇa prādhānyata 'stupid contrivance of scripture with his stolidity of mind...' Maheshvara Tirtha

'If Ravana is stupid enough to distort scriptures how then can his - devotee-goddess relation - with Seetha can be established...' is the question of Rama Tilaka. Thus, it is concluded that Ravana's advances are only with a lecherous intent, contrary to what Maheshvara Tiirtha tried to establish Ravana as a devotee... Tilaka.
In spite of all these debates and counter-debates of commentators - Ravana remained as a devotee of Seetha, namely Goddess Lakshmi, legendarily.

glosses.meaning: for scriptural canons, by you, detrimental, caused by

verses.devanagari:
एतौ पादौ मया स्निग्धौ शिरोभिः परिपीडितौ
प्रसादम् कुरु मे क्षिप्रम् वश्यो दासो अहम् अस्मि ते |
verses.iast:
etau pādau mayā snigdhau śirobhiḥ paripīḍitau
prasādam kuru me kṣipram vaśyo dāso aham asmi te |
verses.translation: "Let these two feet of yours be massaged by my ten heads, do me favour readily, for I am your subordinate and servant. [3-55-35b. 36a]

glosses.meaning: by me, with [ten] heads, let let hem be massaged - let them be touched
I, to you, under control - subordinate

verses.devanagari:
इमाः शून्या मया वाचः शुष्यमाणेन भाषिताः
न च अपि रावणः कांचित् मूर्ध्ना स्त्रीम् प्रणमेत ह |
verses.iast:
imāḥ śūnyā mayā vācaḥ śuṣyamāṇena bhāṣitāḥ
na ca api rāvaṇaḥ kāṃcit mūrdhnā strīm praṇameta ha |
verses.translation: "I with a lustful hollow-heart spoke all these hollow words that are unbefitting to my stature, indeed, Ravana will never supplicate headlong to whosoever woman.
notes: Here the expression śunyāḥ is held inconvenient to derive proper meaning and another ancient mms is said to have this as: na imāḥ śūnyāḥ kṛthā vācaḥ śuṣyamāṇena bhāṣitāḥ where the wordage is śunnyamānena emptied by lust...' imāḥ vācaḥ 'these words...' śūnyāḥ 'empty...' na kṛthā 'do not make them...' 'Nullified by lust I spoke all these words... and you, on taking them as mere nullities, pray, do not nullify my lovelorn words...' Tiirtha calls this as rasābhāsa 'desiring an undesirous woman of others, by hook or by crook.

glosses.itrans: muurdhnaa na ca api praNameta ha
glosses.iast: mūrdhnā na ca api praṇameta ha
glosses.devanagari: मूर्ध्ना न च अपि प्रणमेत ह
glosses.meaning: headlong, not [never,] also, even, supplicate, indeed.

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्त्वा दशग्रीवो मैथिलीम् जनक आत्मजाम् |
कृत अन्त वशम् आपन्नो मम इयम् इति मन्यते
verses.iast:
evam uktvā daśagrīvo maithilīm janaka ātmajām |
kṛta anta vaśam āpanno mama iyam iti manyate
verses.translation: That Decahedral Ravana on speaking thus to Maithili, who is the daughter of Janaka, deemed that 'she is mine,' as he has gone under the sway of the Terminator.
